name: MIC5365-1.0YC5-TR
title: 150 mA single low-dropout regulator, fixed output, with enable
summary: MIC5365 and MIC5366 are CMOS linear regulators that run from 2.5 V to 5.5 V and deliver up to 150 mA at a fixed output from 1.0 V to 3.3 V, chosen by part number. They need only 1 µF ceramic capacitors at input and output, draw 29 µA of ground current, and draw almost nothing when EN is pulled low. The MIC5366 adds a switch that pulls the output to ground while the part is disabled. Current limiting and thermal shutdown protect the part; packages are a 1 mm × 1 mm 4-lead TDFN, 5-lead SC-70 and (MIC5365 only) 5-lead TSOT23.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: A battery feeds VIN directly, with a 1 µF capacitor from VIN to ground beside the part. A second 1 µF capacitor sits on VOUT, which supplies the load (processor I/O, a vibrator motor, a receiver or synthesiser). EN is brought out as its own control input. All grounds return to one node.

operation.text: VIN feeds an LDO block whose output is VOUT; EN drives both the LDO block and a reference that feeds the LDO. In the MIC5366 an auto-discharge block sits between VOUT and GND.

Both devices are 150 mA, low-noise LDOs with linear current limiting and thermal shutdown. The MIC5366 adds an output discharge switch, turned on whenever EN disables the regulator; its resistance is 30 Ω typical. The output voltage is fixed by part number.

A 1 µF capacitor from VIN to ground is needed for stability. Low-ESR ceramic parts work best in the least space; X5R or X7R dielectric is the choice, since Y5V loses most of its value over temperature. Small extra capacitors of NPO dielectric help with high-frequency noise in RF circuits.

VOUT needs at least 1 µF to stay stable, and the loop is tuned for a 1 µF low-ESR ceramic; capacitors with high ESR can cause high-frequency oscillation. More capacitance is allowed but gives little improvement. X7R and X5R are the dielectrics to use: X7R moves about 15 % over its temperature range, while Z5U and Y5V move up to 50 % and 60 %, so a Y5V part must be much larger to keep the same minimum value over temperature.
The regulator stays stable and in regulation with no load at all, which suits keep-alive supplies for CMOS RAM.

EN is active high and is a CMOS input. Pulling it low shuts the regulator down, and its supply current falls almost to zero (0.05 µA typical). Pulling it high turns the output on. EN must not be left floating, or the output state is undefined. Low is 0.2 V or less and high is 1.2 V or more; turn-on takes 50 µs typical.

The part delivers 150 mA continuously in a very small package; the allowed ambient follows from the dissipation and θJA. With 3.6 V in, 2.8 V out and 150 mA, the regulator dissipates 0.120 W; on a minimum-footprint layout (θJA = 250°C/W) the TDFN then runs at up to 95°C ambient. The dissipation limit must not be exceeded. Two θJA figures are published for TSOT23-5: 253°C/W and 235°C/W.

The TDFN carries a two-character code and the SC-70 and TSOT23 a three-character code (see the part numbers). A dot or triangle marks pin 1. The packages are Pb-free; the JEDEC matte-tin symbol appears on the outer packaging.

TSOT23 body sizes leave out mold flash and gate burr, and the outline follows JEDEC MO193 issue C. SC-70 sizes include plating and leave out mold flash and metal burr. The TDFN has a laser-marked pin 1 on top.
